approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local graph genetic algorithm whose oracle budget is spent by a Gaussian-process Thompson sampler, with one stagnation response added on top. Each announced batch of ten it breeds a fresh field of a hundred and sixty de novo offspring from the best scored molecules of the current session by connected-fragment crossover or short random graph edits, rejecting anything that is not a single ordinary connected graph, is already known, or widens its parents' sulfur environments. It fits a Gaussian process to this session's accepted scores alone, using integer-count radius-two Morgan fingerprints under a generalized Tanimoto kernel, and draws one correlated posterior sample across the whole field for each of the ten batch positions. The ten molecules it sends to the oracle are the sequential maxima of those sampled rows: each position takes the largest sampled value among the members still available and the winner is removed before the next position, so a candidate the model rates poorly on average can still buy a position when its sampled residual is large. The one thing this Parent added over its own predecessor is a stagnation-conditioned eligibility rule: it counts consecutive announced batches that failed to raise the session's best score, and while that counter stands at three or more only the forty highest posterior-mean members of the unchanged hundred-and-sixty-member field may compete, the full field returning on the first improving batch. The sampling law itself was left untouched by that change: inside the restricted forty the draw still decides, and in the four hundred and thirty-five batches it actually ran the restriction applied to eighty-eight of them.
approach.novelty: This node removes, for the first time on this Parent, the one thing the draw does: it lets the sampled residual no longer decide who is bought. Each position still runs over exactly the same eligible set, under exactly the same stagnation rule, but takes the member with the highest fitted posterior mean instead of the member with the highest sampled value, while the covariance, its Cholesky factor, the jitter ladder and all ten standard-normal rows are still drawn and consumed in the same order as inert computations, so the random stream never moves. That makes this the greedy end of the Anchor's own pricing axis, measured where the mask lives rather than borrowed from the mask-free Parent where mean-only allocation was last priced. No sibling on this Parent has done it: they scaled the residual up and down during stalls, drew and threw away an extra block of randomness without changing any rule, released the eligibility restriction after five batches, recalibrated the model's far-field uncertainty, or changed what the pool was filled with. Every one of those kept the sampled maximum as the buyer. A second property is worth stating in advance rather than discovering afterwards: because the eligible forty always contains the ten highest posterior means, a mean-only buyer is indifferent to the restriction, so this arm simultaneously shows what the stagnation mask is worth once the draw is gone, which is nothing at all by construction. It is registered as a measurement: a loss, a gain and no material effect are equally the answer.

observed_bottleneck: The behaviour that limits this Parent is how it prices candidates: it buys with a sampled residual rather than with a priced expectation, and the campaign still cannot say what that draw is worth on this Anchor. Recounted read-only from the Anchor's own receipts (runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-61b9b3bfb40d/seed-0|1|2/logs/<task>.log, all 435 announced batches of the fifteen sessions, pool size exactly 160 in 435 of 435 and no numerical fallback), the sampled maximum departs from the posterior-mean maximum of its own available set at 3,733 of 4,350 selection positions (712 of 880 inside the stalled regime, 3,021 of 3,470 outside it), and the emitted ten match the top ten of the (-posterior mean, pool index) ordering as a set in only 3 of 435 batches and in order in none. That draw costs the Anchor measurable model value at purchase: per announced batch the ten picks carry 4.00859 of summed posterior mean against 4.25037 for the top-ten mean order on the same pools (lower in 435 of 435 batches) and 0.38106 of summed posterior SD against 0.28049, and 199 purchases (198 outside the regime, 1 inside) come from the top posterior-SD decile while the mean-only rule on those same pools would have taken none. Outside the stalled regime 997 of 3,470 picks sit at posterior-mean rank 40 or worse (mean rank 31.274, median 15, single picks as deep as rank 157 at batch one); inside it the inherited top-forty mask already removes that tail entirely (0 of 880, mean rank 11.697, median 8). Round 45 measured the consequence of that pricing three times on this same Anchor without being able to price the draw itself: making the far field's uncertainty comparable bought extra calls that converted at a quarter of the inherited rate and lost 0.081702 (n-907d480bc1fe), reserving a fifth of every batch for the archive-far half converted at 0.40x and lost 0.031639 (n-82195b802723), and filling a quarter of the pool with corpus chemistry the surrogate gave no premium lost 0.051941 (n-d527b3b4e2cb); the eligibility axis itself is now bracketed from the loose side by n-5911390da209, whose five-batch release of the mask lost 0.000562. What is missing is the other bracket. The only number the campaign has for removing the sampled draw is -0.116317 on the mask-free Parent n-1744a1494180 (n-f04cec6ab705), and the registered criterion c-masked-residual-influence-contribution refuses it as transferable because on this Anchor the draw can only reorder the top forty posterior means in 88 of 435 batches. The two stall-time amplitude arms (n-189cd716f027 at -0.009718, n-137ec411f54c at -0.003338) varied how large the residual is, never whether it decides, and the two law-free draws (n-47993ce5d053, n-843b25e73dee) attribute nothing to it. Without this Anchor's own departure cost for the draw, a loss from this round's improvement-pricing arm cannot be told apart from 'any move toward the posterior-mean order costs this much here', and a gain cannot be told apart from 'the draw was simply not needed'. Since round 45 the Anchor has its own law-free reference (n-515ab49db6e0, panel -0.020452, band [-0.055482, +0.014579]), so the condition this criterion was waiting on is met.

literature_review.conclusion: No literature is adopted for this node. The intervention is an internal-evidence ablation that removes sampled residual influence from the masked Anchor to supply the greedy bound the other positions of this round are read against.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: This is a registered removal of an inherited component with no new asset, dependency, model or method, and the direction is fixed by the frozen ticket. The design is fully determined by campaign receipts: the implementation principle is published on this lineage (n-f04cec6ab705, n-299096e31fe7), the comparator band is this Anchor's own law-free reference n-515ab49db6e0, and every preregistered forecast in this intent was recomputed read-only from the Anchor's own trajectories and logs. No external source is adopted, so no adoption is claimed; the round's frozen Search Policy review is cited only to record that its candidate methods belong to the other positions of this portfolio and none of them is implemented here.

hypothesis: Remove sampled residual influence on successful choice (m-000000000006) from the masked Anchor's correlated Thompson allocation, and nothing else. At every successful selection position the winner becomes the available pool member with the maximum fitted posterior mean under the inherited ascending-index first-maximum tie rule, instead of the member with the maximum value in that position's correlated sample row; the chosen member is masked out before the next position exactly as before. The full count covariance, its bounded pool Cholesky factor with its inherited jitter ladder, the score_scale residual amplitude, the single (10, 160) standard-normal array drawn from the same generator at the same control-flow point, the resulting sample rows and their finite guard all remain, drawn and consumed in the same order, as passive computations that route no choice and keep the random stream position and the numerical-failure routing identical. The stall-conditioned eligible set is inherited untouched (K=3 consecutive non-improving announced batches, M=40 of 160 by (-posterior mean, pool index), effective size min(M, pool size), full field restored on the first improving batch), so the removal is measured inside the restriction rather than against it. Because every pool holds 160 members and the effective mask of 40 therefore always contains the ten highest posterior means, the emitted batch under this rule is the top ten of the posterior-mean ordering whether or not the batch is restricted: the mask stays present, audited and non-binding, and the measured endpoint is the total departure cost of the draw on this Anchor.

finding_summary.headline: Removing the sampled draw on the masked Anchor costs -0.126894, and reproduces the mask-free removal exactly
finding_summary.insights:
The registered question is answered on the Anchor that carries the mask. Sampled residual influence is strongly load-bearing here: removing it costs 0.126894 of panel mean, far beyond the 0.002 descriptive scale and far outside this Anchor's own law-free departure band, so the conditional contribution of the draw is positive and large. The campaign no longer has to borrow the mask-free number: the masked figure is larger, not smaller, than the -0.116317 it refused as transferable, which settles the round's framing question in the opposite direction from the one the restriction argument suggested.

What makes the answer unusually clean is also what limits it. Because the removal reproduces the mask-free removal exactly, the -0.126894 is the cost of departing from this Anchor to one specific greedy destination, and it cannot be split into a residual term and a mask term - both the draw and the mask stop operating at that same destination. The corollary is a new fact about the mask itself: the stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility rule, whose +0.010577 made this Anchor, is worth exactly nothing once the draw is gone, not approximately nothing but identically nothing, demonstrated by an equal realization rather than argued from pool arithmetic. Whatever that rule contributes is wholly conditional on a sampled residual being present to restrict. That is a direct, if partial, answer to the open question about whether the mask's margin is real: it is at best a property of the sampled regime, and it is zero outside it. It still says nothing about intermediate residual amplitudes or about other values of the mask size, where the restriction could bind.

For this round's other arms the greedy bound is now in hand at the same path realization: an improvement- or dispersion-based pricing arm that loses materially less than 0.126894 is buying something the pure posterior mean does not, and one that lands near it has merely rediscovered the mean order. The pricing diagnosis the campaign recorded - that this stack's limitation is candidate pricing and ranking - survives this test with its sign fixed: the fix is not to remove dispersion from the buy.

On the method itself, the trajectories and the molecular report converge on one diagnosis, and the receipts support it. Buying strictly by posterior mean turns the search into sustained local refinement of whichever skeleton the surrogate currently likes: distinct Murcko scaffolds per session fall to 54.9 from the Parent's 117.5 (lower in 14 of 15 matched sessions), mean pairwise Tanimoto rises to 0.432 from 0.296 (higher in 15 of 15), the single most common scaffold takes 39.9 per cent of a session's proposals against 18.9, near-duplicate proposals rise to 10.5 per cent from 1.4, and one session spent 290 proposals on 15 scaffolds with 76 per cent on one. None of that is visible to the string-uniqueness check, which still reports 864-875 unique strings of 870 on every objective - a caution for any future node that reads uniqueness as diversity. The allocation receipts are the mechanism of that collapse: every purchase in the mean head, top-SD-decile purchases down from 199 to 8, summed purchased SD down to 0.158 from the 0.268 the sampled rule would have taken on the same pools. The downstream signature matches - almost the same number of incumbent improvements with a third less mass, which is what a halogen walk around a frozen skeleton produces. There is a second, weaker reading worth flagging: within its own top ten the surrogate's prospective rank correlation with realized score averages 0.375 and is negative in 64 of 435 batches (the Anchor's is 0.515, negative in 30), so the fine ordering the greedy rule spends the whole budget on is only weakly informative at that resolution. That figure is deflated by the narrow score spread inside a top-ten batch and should not be read as a like-for-like comparison. The limitation this prices is a property of the purchase rule, not of the proposal operators: what would remove it is a ranking model or acquisition that keeps a dispersion or diversity term in the buy - expected improvement with a risk term, a batch rule with an explicit scaffold-novelty or determinantal diversity penalty, or a surrogate whose uncertainty is not a function of archive similarity - rather than any retuning of the residual's amplitude, which two earlier arms already showed moves the endpoint by only -0.009718 and -0.003338.

What stays open: whether any part of the 0.126894 can be recovered by a pricing rule that is deterministic but not mean-greedy; whether the mask has value at intermediate residual amplitudes, where it could actually bind; and whether the loss is partly a property of this one dependent realization - three seeds, thirteen of fifteen cells down, with two cells carrying 0.588 of the 1.903 of lost increment mass. This route should not iterate: it is a control that reached its registered destination, it is not a candidate improvement, and repeating mean-only allocation on this Parent would buy nothing new. The goal it serves stays open for the eight retained identities on this Anchor whose contribution is still unmeasured.
finding_summary.results:
The removal executed cleanly on all three seeds and every pre-registered observable moved exactly as forecast. All 4,350 oracle calls across the fifteen sessions were the highest posterior mean of their own available set, and all 435 announced batches were exactly the top ten of the posterior-mean ordering; the Anchor's sampled rule had departed from that mean maximum at 3,733 of those 4,350 positions and matched the top-ten set in only 3 of 435 batches. The posterior-mean rank of every purchase collapsed to 0-9 (mean 4.5, maximum 9) in and out of the stalled regime, against the Anchor's in-regime mean rank 11.70 and out-of-regime 31.27 with 997 of 3,470 purchases at rank 40 or worse. Purchases from the top posterior-SD decile fell from 199 to 8 of 4,350. On the node's own pools the ten bought carried 3.4248 of summed posterior mean against 3.2282 for the sampled rule replayed on the same pool and mask (higher in 434 of 435 batches) and 0.1583 of summed posterior SD against 0.2684 (lower in 432 of 435). The random stream, the model arithmetic and the inherited eligibility rule were untouched: one 10-by-160 standard-normal array per batch in the same place and order, pool size 160 in every batch, no numerical fallback, the stall counter reproduced from the node's own accepted scores with no mismatch, and the retained mask binding in none of the 435 batches. At each session's single same-state first batch the pools, means, SDs, score scale, jitters and all ten normal rows were identical to the Anchor's, the removal displaced exactly 132 of 150 of the Anchor's picks with every one of the fifteen per-session counts as forecast, the average posterior mean of the ten bought rose in all fifteen, and the passive replay of the old sampled rule reproduced the Anchor's own ten in all fifteen.

Downstream, realized incumbent-increment mass fell from 5.9781 to 4.0747, a 31.8 per cent loss, spread over almost the same number of improvement events (250 against 253): each improvement simply got smaller. Inside the stalled regime the mass fell from 0.5470 to 0.2112.

The endpoint panel is complete and paired on seeds 0/1/2 across all five tasks: macro 0.480136 against the Anchor's 0.607030, a paired loss of 0.126894. Seed macros fell by 0.233405, 0.061951 and 0.085327; thirteen of fifteen cells fell and two rose (median_2 seed 0 +0.012805, zaleplon_mpo seed 0 +0.004139). Task means: sitagliptin_mpo -0.258049, drd2_docking -0.246948, deco_hop -0.116224, zaleplon_mpo -0.013731, median_2 +0.000481. The two fragile high cells are included, not excluded: deco_hop seed 0 fell from 0.856148 to 0.595220 and sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 from 0.765861 to 0.438199. Against this Anchor's own law-free band of [-0.055482, +0.014579] around -0.020452, the -0.126894 sits 2.3 times below the band's lower edge, so the loss is not a plausible path-departure realization; the three median_2 cells all sit inside that task's own band.

One result was not predicted and is the most consequential. This node's fifteen scored trajectories are identical record for record - all 4,500 molecules, same SMILES, same scores - to the mask-free mean-only removal the campaign ran on the previous Parent, and its macro mean, three seed macros and five task means match to full precision. The two programs are different: this one carries the whole stall-mask machinery and exercised it in 116 of 435 batches, the other has no mask at all. Because a mean-only buyer always finds the ten highest posterior means inside the eligible forty, the mask never bound once, so the two removals land on exactly the same realization. The entire difference between this Anchor's departure cost of -0.126894 and the mask-free -0.116317 is -0.010577, which is precisely the Anchor's own published gain over its mask-free Parent.

molecular.headline: Aromatic, ring-rich molecules that walk halogens around one scaffold per session; trioxides, cyclobutadienes and N-halogen amines sit at the top
molecular.overall_character: Across all 15 sessions the node emits flat, heavily aromatic, heavily halogenated molecules of 345-711 Da that are overwhelmingly rearrangements of the ten initial pool members. The digest counters support the ring and aromatic reading: ring_closure_rate is 0.9989-1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9989-1.0 on every one of the five objectives, and my own RDKit read of the 4,350 proposed molecules gives a mean of 3.0-5.5 rings and 2.0-4.9 aromatic rings per molecule. Nothing is charged (charged_rate 0.0 everywhere) and nothing is stereodefined (stereocentre_rate 0.0 everywhere). Almost every string is unique (864-875 unique of 870 proposed per objective), but the uniqueness is cosmetic: the differences between consecutive proposals are single halogen or heteroatom swaps on a frozen skeleton. Measured against the code Parent's matched sessions, this node runs 54.9 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 290-molecule session versus the Parent's 117.5 (fewer in 14 of 15 matched pairs), a mean pairwise Morgan Tanimoto of 0.432 versus 0.296 (higher in all 15 of 15 matched pairs), a most-common-scaffold share of 0.399 versus 0.189, and a near-duplicate rate (a proposal within Tanimoto 0.9 of an earlier proposal in the same session) of 10.5% versus 1.4%. The molecules are, by every reading I can take, markedly more similar to each other within a session than the Anchor's are. The chemistry they buy on the way up is decoration, not design: halogen identity, O-for-S, amide-for-amidine, and extra ring-closure digits that produce strained or bridged rings a chemist cannot make.

per_task.generated_character: The smallest and most uniform set of the five: mean SMILES length 44.8, max 77, and essentially every molecule is the same 3-ring, 345-425 Da indole-2-carboxanilide inherited from initial molecule 9. My RDKit read gives a flat 2.99-3.00 rings per molecule in all three sessions, all aromatic ([5,6,6] sizes), and the single Murcko scaffold O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1 covers 48%, 58% and 71% of the three sessions' proposals, with only 42, 34 and 23 distinct scaffolds per session against the Parent's 77, 74 and 73. halogen_rate is 0.9931, so almost every molecule carries at least one halogen, and the halogens are the decoration being bought.
liabilities: N-halogen amines and amidines (N(F), N(Cl), N(Br) on the anilide nitrogen) in 59% and 76% of two of the three sessions; these are electrophilic halogenating agents, not stable anilides
benzylic halomethyl groups CCl and CBr as the top-scoring decoration; alkylating and not a substituent a chemist would install
free amidine C(=N)N substituted for the amide in the best molecules, which changes the compound class rather than refining it
degenerate single-atom and two-atom proposals such as Br scoring 0.0 and Fc1ccc(F)cc1 scoring 2.2e-13 spent as evaluations
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere in these sessions, although the objective's own lower-scoring pool members carry one
no saturated basic ring nitrogen in any of the three sessions (0.0 by my substructure count on all unique molecules)
no stereocentres at all, with digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 over 870 proposals
no N-acyl-N-alkyl amine or any flexible polar side chain; the set is three fused aromatic rings and nothing else
no second heteroaromatic ring system; the indole nitrogen is the only ring heteroatom in most proposals
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC already scores 0.3051 at evaluation 9, and 870 proposals buy only +0.122 on top of it, to a ceiling of 0.4276. What climbs is small: trading one methoxy for methyl, hanging a halomethyl on the ring, and swapping the amide C(=O) for an amidine C(=N). Above about 0.425 the gradient is flat - the twelve best molecules in the digest all sit at 0.4276 or 0.4257 and differ only in which halogen occupies the same two positions (CCl/CF/CBr on the ring methyl, N(F)/N(Cl)/N(Br) on the anilide nitrogen). The objective is no longer distinguishing them, and the optimizer spends its last 150 evaluations on that indifference.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the five: mean SMILES length 78.7, max 142, and my RDKit read gives mean molecular weights of 711, 486 and 632 Da across the three sessions with 4.0-5.0 rings, almost all aromatic (aromatic_atom_rate 1.0, ring_closure_rate 1.0). The family is the dimethyl purine-dione from initial molecule 7, grown by hanging more heteroaryl rings and esters on it until the best molecule reaches 628 Da with 5 aromatic rings, 12 rotatable bonds and zero hydrogen-bond donors. This is the most converged objective in the node: 23, 15 and 35 distinct Murcko scaffolds per session against the Parent's 126, 124 and 102, with the top scaffold holding 40%, 76% and 63% of proposals and near-duplicate rates of 46%, 12% and 38% against the Parent's 0.3%, 3% and 0.7%.
liabilities: polyoxide chains: an O-O-O sequence appears in 209 of 300 records in one session and in 41% of another, and the single best molecule in the digest carries OOOC, a methyl trioxide that is not an isolable compound
thionoesters C(=S)OCC appearing as a free swap for the ethyl ester in the top-scoring set
enol ether C=C(O...) termini carried by every one of the twelve best molecules
cyclopentadiene and cyclopentene substituents (C2=CCC=C2) that are tautomerically unstable as aryl replacements
missing_features: no basic amine of any kind in two of three sessions (0.3% and 3.4% of unique molecules)
no saturated nitrogen heterocycle at all in any of the three sessions
no stereocentres, with digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 870 proposals
no hydrogen-bond donor on the best molecule, and no polar handle beyond esters and ring carbonyls
no reduction in size as the score rises; the objective is not rewarding anything that trims the 628 Da, 12-rotatable-bond top molecule
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Everything scores at least 0.5 - the digest's worst molecule on this objective is 0.5385 and the median is 0.5849 - so the whole 870-molecule run lives in a 0.099-wide window and the reported climb from 0.5447 to 0.5990 is a thin ridge. Within that ridge the score rises with sheer aromatic mass: adding a pyrimidinyl ring, a butyl pyridine and an ethyl ester to the purine-dione takes 0.5484 to 0.5990. Crucially, the twelve best molecules are all 0.5989554700384827 to the last digit, and they differ by the length of a peroxide chain (OOOC vs OOOCC vs OOOCCC), an ester oxygen swapped for sulfur, or a methyl swapped for chloromethyl. The gradient stopped resolving them and the optimizer kept buying.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: This objective has by far the widest span the node saw: 0.0004 to 0.9421 with a median of 0.2350. The bottom is unambiguous - the lowest-scoring molecules are all the inherited biaryl acid with a sulfonylated pyrrolidine amide, scoring 0.0116 to 0.0190, where the only nitrogens are an amide N and a sulfonamide N and the molecule carries a free carboxylic acid. The top is equally clear: every molecule above 0.86 pairs a free, unacylated basic amine on a small saturated ring with a halogenated aryl ring a short linker away, and drops the acid and the sulfonyl entirely. Seed 0's ceiling of 0.3848 is what that family can reach without making that move: its best molecule replaces the pyrrolidine with a 1,3-diazetidine but leaves the only ring nitrogen sulfonylated, so the basic centre is reduced to a primary CH2NH2 on an indene-type 5-6-6 carbocycle, and the molecule carries 5 hydrogen-bond donors at 490 Da. Its score climbed monotonically (0.019 at eval 10, 0.145 at 100, 0.256 at 150, 0.350 at 250, 0.385 at 300) and its last eight proposals are still the same sulfonamide with a different halogen on the aryl - it was still decorating, not re-scaffolding, when the budget ran out. It explored 81 distinct scaffolds against the Parent's 136.

per_task.score_gradient_reading: The widest dynamic range and the harshest floor in the node: best 0.5102, median 0.1909, worst 4.8e-27, with fragments like FCF scoring 1.4e-22 and C1=C(c2ccccc2)CC1 scoring 6.4e-17. What climbs is fluorine count on a compact, flat bicyclic: the 0.5102 family carries two aryl fluorines in a 1,2-relationship plus an aliphatic C-F and an OCH2F, on a 414 Da four-ring scaffold with three rotatable bonds. The lower seed-2 cage reaches 0.3078 with a single aryl fluorine and a phenol in its place. The twelve best molecules differ only in whether the fluorinated ether is OCF, OCCF or CF and where the ring fluorine sits, so once the fluorine pattern is set the gradient is again flat.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over the 15 matched sessions this node averages 54.9 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 290 proposals against the code Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d's 117.5, lower in 14 of 15 matched pairs; mean pairwise Morgan Tanimoto across each session's proposals averages 0.432 against 0.296 and is higher in 15 of 15 matched pairs; the single most common scaffold holds 39.9% of a session's proposals against 18.9%; and 10.5% of proposals fall within Tanimoto 0.9 of an earlier proposal in the same session against 1.4%. One session ran 290 proposals over 15 scaffolds with 76% of them on one. Yet the digest records 864-875 unique strings of 870 proposed on every objective, so the collapse is at scaffold level and invisible to any string-uniqueness check.
transferable_gaps.gap: Within a session the generator converges onto one scaffold and then only permutes substituents on it, producing molecules markedly more similar to each other than the code Parent's are.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A purchase rule that takes the highest posterior mean at every position buys a halogen-and-heteroatom walk around whichever skeleton the model currently likes best. The generator needs either a diversity-aware or dispersion-aware purchase, or an explicit scaffold-novelty term in what it is allowed to buy, so that distinct ring skeletons remain reachable late in a session. This is a property of how candidates are selected, not of any particular target.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The substring C(F)(F)F appears zero times in all 4,500 trajectory records of this node, and a gem-difluoromethylene matches 0.2% of unique molecules. This is not for lack of halogen: the digest reports halogen_rate 1.0 on one objective, 0.9931 on another and 0.8241 on a third, and my substructure count puts a C-X alkyl halide on 34.5% of unique molecules. Every one of those halogens is a single substitution - one C-F, C-Cl, C-Br, or an N-F/N-Cl/N-Br - and the top-scoring molecules on three objectives differ from each other only by which single halogen sits at one position.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot assemble a multiply-halogenated carbon. It has no trifluoromethyl, and essentially no gem-difluoride, anywhere.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The edit operator appears to set a halogen per atom position rather than insert a substituent group. A generator that cannot place a trifluoromethyl, a difluoromethyl or any other multi-atom substituent as a unit cannot reach a large and ordinary region of medicinal chemistry, no matter what it is being scored on. It needs fragment-level or group-level substituent insertion alongside per-atom mutation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A saturated-ring basic nitrogen appears in 6.4% of this node's unique molecules averaged over the 15 sessions, against 25.2% in the code Parent's matched sessions; a six-membered saturated amine ring in 3.6% against 15.6%; piperazine in zero of 4,350 molecules here and 0.3% of one Parent session. Where it does appear it is decisive: the two molecules that reached 0.886 and 0.942 both carry a free, unacylated amine on a small saturated ring two bonds from a halogenated aryl, while a session that reached only 0.385 kept its only ring nitrogen sulfonylated in 97.2% of its proposals and never produced the unsulfonylated version.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits almost no basic amine centre on a saturated ring, and no piperazine at all, although its own highest-scoring molecules on one panel member carry exactly that.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator can delete or acylate a basic nitrogen but has no reliable operator that installs a saturated amine heterocycle, and no operator that strips an electron-withdrawing group off a nitrogen to restore its basicity. Both of those are single, well-defined edits that a task-agnostic candidate proposer should be able to make on any skeleton.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring content itself is abundant - digest ring_closure_rate is 0.9989 to 1.0 on all five panel members - but three- and four-membered rings appear in 25.6% of unique molecules, and a cyclobutadiene-type ring (two double bonds in a non-aromatic four-ring) appears in 3.3% of this node's molecules against 0.0% of the code Parent's. The single highest-scoring molecule in the node has RDKit ring sizes [4,4,4,6,6]; the second-highest contains C1=CC=C1; another objective's best molecule has ring sizes [4,6,6,8,12] with an eight- and a twelve-membered bridged ring, and 79% of that session's molecules carry a ring larger than seven.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction operates on SMILES ring-closure digits rather than on chemically valid ring templates, so the rings it builds are strained, bridged or antiaromatic rather than ordinary fused bicyclics.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator editing ring-closure tokens can raise a score by creating ring systems no chemist can make, and the scorers do not object. It needs ring edits expressed as insertion, fusion or expansion of valid ring templates, with a post-edit check on ring size and on antiaromatic four-rings, so that ring exploration stays inside makeable chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An O-O-O sequence appears in 209 of 300 records in one session and in 41% of another, and a peroxide bond matches 11.8% of this node's unique molecules against 2.7% of the code Parent's matched sessions. The highest-scoring molecule in one of those sessions carries an OOOC methyl trioxide and the twelve best molecules in that session differ from each other mainly by the length of that chain. It is being actively purchased: once the first peroxide entered, the session's remaining budget went to extending and decorating it.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator freely writes peroxide and polyoxide chains, and nothing in its pipeline rejects them.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A parse-valid string is not a compound. The generator needs a stability filter on the proposals it offers - O-O chains, N-N and N-O singles, N-halogen bonds - applied before a candidate is costed, so that a flat region of an objective cannot be exploited by chemistry that does not exist.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bond appears in 9.9% of this node's unique molecules against 6.2% of the code Parent's, peaking at 59% and 76% of two sessions, and the N-halogen is carried by the very molecules the digest lists as best on one panel member - the twelve top molecules there all have a halogen on an anilide or amidine nitrogen. An N-fluoro imide also appears on the best molecules of one session on a different panel member.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator places halogens on nitrogen as freely as on carbon, producing N-halo amines, amidines and imides at the top of its own rankings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The atom-mutation operator treats halogen as a valid substituent on any heavy atom. It needs valence- and stability-aware atom typing that distinguishes where a halogen is a substituent from where it makes an electrophilic halogenating reagent, applied uniformly and without reference to what is being optimized.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 and charged_rate is 0.0 on all five panel members, across 4,350 proposals. This is not because the molecules are flat: my RDKit read gives 3.0 to 5.5 rings per molecule with substantial sp3 ring-fusion content, and the top-scoring molecules on three panel members each carry two to four sp3 carbons bearing four different substituents, every one of them left unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces no stereochemistry and no ionizable form, over every molecule it has ever proposed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator with no stereo tokens cannot distinguish diastereomers or enantiomers and cannot refine a three-dimensional fit once it has found a two-dimensional one; one with no charged forms cannot represent the protonation state most amines actually occupy. Both are representational, apply to every objective equally, and would have to be added to the candidate string vocabulary and to whatever operator proposes edits.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
